Subject: TTFT & streaming cadence — follow up and next steps

Thanks John — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope a short POC: 

Recap (from discovery)
- Primary UX: streaming chat UI (web) that shows incremental tokens.
- Target TTFT (time-to-first-token) requirement: very important for perceived responsiveness. You mentioned wanting it to feel instant for users.
- Expected request profile: a mix of short (50-200 tokens) and long (800-1,500 tokens) generations, with an average around 1,200 tokens per response.
- Concurrency/scale: you called out ~150 active concurrent users at peak and ~40-60 RPS sustained during business spikes.
- Transport preference: SSE (Server-Sent Events) preferred, but some clients may use WebSocket.

Open questions we need to confirm to size the POC and test plan:
1) TTFT targets: can you confirm p95 and p99 targets for TTFT (time from request to first token arriving in the client)? Example: p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 400ms.
2) Streaming cadence: desired cadence between chunks (ms) and preferred chunk size (tokens/chunk). You mentioned UI-smoothness — do you want ~100–200ms between client-visible chunks?
3) % of requests that actually need streaming vs. ones that can be served as non-streaming (batch)?
4) Are there preferred regions (us-west/us-east/eu) and any compliance constraints we should be aware of?

I attached a quick requirements workbook (acme_ttft_requirements.xlsx) to capture the answers — please fill the highlighted cells and reattach.

Next steps I propose:
- You fill the workbook by Monday -> we propose a 3-day POC (dedicated stage env) to measure p50/p95/p99 TTFT and streaming chunk cadence under synthetic load.
- Laura will follow with a proposed technical test plan.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min sync if that's easier.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — appreciated the clear recap. Answers inline: 

1) TTFT targets: our internal UX team measured acceptable responsiveness as:
   - p95 TTFT <= 200ms
   - p99 TTFT <= 400ms
   Note: for very short responses (<= 50 tokens) we'd like first token under 150ms if possible.

2) Streaming cadence and chunking: we prefer SSE. The UX is happiest when chunks arrive ~100-200ms apart for the first few chunks; after that 200-400ms is OK. We generally plan to stream roughly 40-80 tokens per chunk; client-side will buffer and render at token granularity but we want visible updates every ~150ms on average.

3) % requiring streaming: ~85% of requests should stream. Remaining 15% are server-to-server or scheduled jobs that can be non-streaming.

4) Regions/compliance: primary traffic from us-west / us-east; Acme is OK with hosted solutions (no on-prem required for POC).

Attaching a short client trace from a prototype (client_stream_trace.log) that shows current TTFT and chunk cadence on our side for comparison.

Happy to review the POC plan with Laura.

— John

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming cadence — technical plan & recommendations

Hi John / Marissa — thanks for the notes and the trace. Laura from Solutions Engineering here. High level thoughts and proposed test plan attached (proposed_test_plan.pdf). Highlights below: 

Immediate recommendations to improve TTFT for streaming use cases:
- Warm-up & pool pre-warming: keep a small warm pool to reduce cold-starts for short requests.
- Prompt engineering: minimize local instruction text on every request (use server-side prompt templates / cached prefixes).
- KV cache & prefix caching: use KV caching for repeated contexts to reduce model compute prior to first token.
- Prioritize first-token generation: for some model backends we can optimize beam/decoding hyperparams to return the first token faster (slightly increase total latency but improve TTFT).

Proposed POC test plan (summary):
1) Baseline single-request TTFT: measure p50/p95/p99 TTFT for representative prompts (short, medium, long) from us-west region.
2) Streaming cadence test: open SSE clients and measure time between first-token and subsequent chunks; verify chunk cadence with target 100–200ms for first N chunks.
3) Load/concurrency sweep: run tests at 50, 150, 300 concurrent connections to observe TTFT degradation and tail latency; measure throughput at 40/60/100 RPS.
4) Transport comparison: SSE vs WebSocket vs batched non-streaming for fallbacks.
5) Reporting: generate a metrics dashboard (p50/p95/p99 TTFT, per-chunk inter-arrival times, token throughput, error rates).

POC logistics: 
- Duration: 3 business days of advanced testing, plus 1 day for analysis.
- Environment: dedicated stage infra in us-west for Acme.
- Data: we will not persist any customer inputs beyond the test window; logs retained per agreed policy.

Next ask from Acme: sample prompt set (short/medium/long), example client SSE config (chunk size, heartbeat), and confirmation of peak concurrency window. Once we have that we'll schedule the POC start date.

Attaching the test plan PDF. Happy to jump on a 30-min runbook call to align.

Regards,
